title: China Airlines 676
summary: An Airbus A300 on ILS/DME approach to Taipei was 1000 ft above the normal glide slope. During go-around, the autopilot disengaged but the captain was unaware. The aircraft climbed steeply and stalled at 2751 ft. All 196 people on board were killed when it crashed into a residential area.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the captain was unaware the autopilot had disengaged during go-around and made no input to control the aircraft, which subsequently stalled.

factors.evidence: Aircraft was more than 300 m above its normal altitude and crew continued the approach.
The autopilot was disengaged but the pilot was not aware of it, leaving aircraft under no one's control for 11 seconds.
Pilot did not actively take control during go-around because he thought the autopilot would initiate the maneuver.
Aircraft reached 42.7 degree pitch-up angle with 45 knot speed and stalled at 2751 ft.
Aircraft fell and crashed into ground 200 ft left of runway, hitting houses and exploding.

events.text: Aircraft was 1000 ft too high above glide slope at 1.2 nautical miles short of runway in light rain and fog.
Go-around power applied, landing gear raised, flaps set to 20 degrees as aircraft climbed at 35 degree pitch-up angle.
Aircraft reached 42.7 degree pitch-up angle at 2751 ft with 45 knot speed and stalled.
Aircraft crashed into residential area 200 ft left of runway, hitting houses and exploding with all 196 killed.

notes: go-around at low altitude led to stall

title: 1998 Ariana Afghan Airlines crash
summary: While descending for Kabul International Airport, the Boeing 727 struck the Shakh-e Barantay Mountain at 2600 metres altitude. The weather at the time was bad with poor visibility amid snow and rain. All 45 people aboard perished, comprising 10 crew members and 35 passengers. No formal accident investigation was conducted due to the Taliban regime's international isolation and loss of the aircraft's black boxes.

factors.evidence: The weather at the time of the accident was bad, with poor visibility amid snow and rain
During descent for landing, the aircraft struck terrain on a route to Kabul International Airport
the flight struck the Shakh-e Barantay Mountain at an altitude of 2600 m at 13:00 local time

events.text: The unscheduled flight was descending for Kabul International Airport.
The weather at the time of the accident was bad, with poor visibility amid snow and rain in the landing approach area.
The flight struck the Shakh-e Barantay Mountain at an altitude of 2600 m at 13:00 local time.

notes: No investigation report; black boxes not recovered; Taliban isolation prevented formal investigation

title: Cubana de Aviación 389
summary: The Tu-154M overran the runway during takeoff from Quito after the nose failed to rotate at VR speed. The aircraft experienced two failed takeoff attempts before a third attempt was made. During the final attempt the nose would not lift despite reaching VR speed, forcing a rejected takeoff that the aircraft could not stop in time. The aircraft overran and crashed into buildings and a soccer field where post-crash fire killed many survivors.
probable_cause: When the aircraft reached VR speed on the third takeoff attempt, the nose of the aircraft would not rotate. The crew rejected the takeoff but the aircraft overran the runway end.

factors.evidence: When Flight 389 reached VR speed, the nose of the aircraft wouldn't rotate (lift)
During the first engine start a pneumatic valve was blocked; two engines were started with ground power and third engine started during taxi
The aircraft overran the runway, narrowly missed the heavily traveled Tufiño avenue, slammed into a wall, clipped an auto mechanic shop, smashed into two houses and plowed into a soccer field
The aircraft exploded and burst into flames; the post-crash fire was more determinant in the tragedy than the actual runway overrun

events.text: During first engine start a pneumatic valve was blocked; the problem was rectified and two engines started with ground power
Third engine was started during taxi as aircraft prepared for takeoff
Flight 389 obtained takeoff clearance and started first takeoff roll which then failed
Second takeoff attempt commenced and then failed before VR speed reached
Third takeoff attempt made and aircraft reached VR speed but nose of aircraft wouldn't rotate (lift)
Crew initiated rejected takeoff procedure but aircraft overran the runway at the end
Aircraft slammed into wall, mechanic shop, two houses and plowed into soccer field; aircraft exploded and burst into flames

notes: Root cause of takeoff failure not stated in text

title: Swissair 111
summary: Swissair Flight 111, an MD-11 flying from New York to Geneva, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean off Peggys Cove, Nova Scotia, on 2 September 1998 after smoke was detected in the cockpit and the crew diverted toward Halifax, killing all 229 aboard. Canada's TSB found that flammable material in the aircraft's structure let the fire spread beyond the crew's control; following the smoke checklist, the crew shut off the cabin bus and recirculation fans, which let the fire reach the cockpit and disable the flight instruments and autopilot before the aircraft struck the water.
probable_cause: The TSB concluded that flammable material used in the aircraft's structure allowed an in-flight fire to spread beyond the flight crew's control, disabling flight instruments and the autopilot and leading to loss of control before impact with the ocean.

factors.evidence: Flammable material used in the aircraft's structure allowed a fire to spread beyond the control of the flight crew, resulting in the crash of the aircraft.
The flight crew detected an odour in the cockpit and determined it to be smoke from the air conditioning system, and smoke became visible four minutes later.

In accordance with the Swissair checklist 'Smoke/fumes of unknown origin', the flight crew shut off power to the cabin using the 'CABIN BUS' switch, which also turned off the recirculating fans, allowing the fire to spread to the cockpit.
In a smoke-filled cockpit and with almost no flight instruments and little to no view outside, Löw may have become spatially disoriented.
Flight 111 struck the ocean at an estimated speed of 345 mph near St. Margarets Bay, killing all 215 passengers and 14 crew members on board.

events.text: At 22:10 ADT while flying over Yarmouth, Nova Scotia, the flight crew detected an odour in the cockpit and determined it was smoke from the air conditioning system.
Four minutes later the odour returned and smoke became visible, prompting the pilots to make a pan-pan call to Moncton Centre and request a diversion.

Following the Swissair 'Smoke/fumes of unknown origin' checklist, the crew shut off power to the cabin using the CABIN BUS switch, which also turned off the recirculating fans and allowed the fire to spread toward the cockpit.
At 22:24:28 the crew reported 'we now must fly manually' as the fire cut power to the autopilot, then declared an emergency ten seconds later in the last transmission received from Flight 111.

In a smoke-filled cockpit with almost no flight instruments, First Officer Löw may have become spatially disoriented, and the aircraft struck the ocean near St. Margarets Bay at an estimated 345 mph at 22:31:18 ADT.

title: 1998 Lignes Aériennes Congolaises crash
summary: The aircraft took off from Kindu Airport and began initial climb on a domestic passenger flight to Kinshasa. Three minutes after takeoff, Tutsi rebels fired a missile that struck one of the aircraft's rear engines. The pilot heard firing and reported the hit to air traffic control before reporting the engines were on fire and the plane was becoming uncontrollable. The aircraft crashed in jungle with all 40 to 41 occupants killed. Tutsi rebels admitted shooting down the aircraft, claiming it was carrying military supplies.
probable_cause: Aircraft shot down by Tutsi rebel forces using a missile during initial climb.

factors.evidence: Tutsi rebels admitted that they had shot down the plane
The missile had reportedly struck one of the aircraft's rear engines
the plane becoming uncontrollable and that he would attempt to land the aircraft
plane becoming uncontrollable

events.text: At 08:51, the aircraft took off from Kindu Airport for a flight to Kinshasa.
The pilot immediately replied that he had heard firing and would call back to confirm his report.
The pilot called back, confirming that the aircraft had been hit three minutes after takeoff, and issued an SOS.
In the last contact, the pilot informed ATC that the plane's engines were on fire and the plane was becoming uncontrollable.

title: Thai Airways International 261
summary: Domestic flight stalled and crashed into a swamp during third landing attempt after multiple go-arounds. Crew became upset after repeated failed approaches, causing disorientation. During go-around the angle of attack gradually increased to 48 degrees, leading to aerodynamic stall and loss of control into the swamp.
probable_cause: Crew disorientation and loss of situational awareness after multiple failed landing attempts, resulting in inadequate monitoring of aircraft attitude.

factors.evidence: the pilots attempted to land the aircraft but then decided to go-around for a second approach
the visibility decreased from 1,500 to 1,000 m which was now less than allowed for the type of non-precision approach in use
the crew became upset, causing them not to maintain awareness of the condition of their aircraft
During the go-around, the angle of attack of the aircraft gradually increased from 18 degrees to 48 degrees
the pilots failed to recover the aircraft and the aircraft crashed into the swamp

events.text: At 18:42 local time, the runway was sighted and the pilots attempted to land the aircraft
They then decided to go-around for a second approach
At 19:05 local time, the flight crews were informed of the weather in the area, which had deteriorated, with visibility decreased from 1,500 to 1,000 m
During the go-around, the angle of attack of the aircraft gradually increased from 18 degrees to 48 degrees
The pilots failed to recover the aircraft and the aircraft crashed into the swamp
